questions.q: What are the three components that make up the set of integers?
questions.a: Integers consist of positive whole numbers, negative whole numbers, and zero. A wrong answer (like saying they include fractions) reveals a confusion between integers and rational numbers.

questions.q: If the temperature in a city is -5°C and in another city it is -2°C, which city is colder? Explain why.
questions.a: The city at -5°C is colder. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks -5 is "more" than -2 because 5 is greater than 2, failing to realize that negative numbers represent values further from zero in the "less than" direction.

questions.q: A bank account has a balance of 0. If you withdraw 500 rupees, how would you represent your new balance using an integer?
questions.a: The balance is -500 rupees. The steps involve identifying 0 as the start and "withdrawal" as a decrease, requiring a negative sign. A wrong answer shows a misunderstanding of how negative signs represent "below zero" or debt.

questions.q: Compare the two numbers -10 and -1. Which is greater, and how does their position on the number line prove it?
questions.a: -1 is greater than -10. On a number line, any number to the right of another is greater; since -1 is closer to zero and to the right of -10, it is the larger value. A wrong answer indicates the student is ignoring the negative sign when comparing magnitudes.

questions.q: Is zero a positive or a negative integer? Defend your answer.
questions.a: Zero is neither positive nor negative; it is the neutral reference point. A wrong answer indicates a misunderstanding of the "boundary" nature of zero in the number system.

questions.q: Create a real-life scenario where you would need to use a negative number, and explain what zero would represent in that specific scenario.
questions.a: An example is measuring altitude: a mountain peak is +500m, while a valley is -100m; zero represents the sea level. A poor answer would be one that describes a quantity that cannot be negative, such as "number of people in a room," showing a lack of understanding of what negative numbers represent (opposite directions/states).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Integers are a set of numbers that include all positive counting numbers (1, 2, 3...), their negative ______ (-1, -2, -3...), and zero.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are in an elevator of a building with a ______.
What is Integers? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Integers are a set of numbers that include all positive counting numbers (1, 2, 3...), their negative counterparts (-1, -2, -3...), and zero.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: When you press the '______' button, you are at the ground level (the Welcome Hall).
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Integers?
questions.a: Students often believe that -10 is "bigger" than -1 because 10 is bigger than 1.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify integers on a number line, compare their values (knowing that -5 is smaller than -2), and represent real-world situations (like temperature or bank balances) using positive and negative signs.
